symptom: On Studio Pro 11.15.0-rc.4 every `alter microflow … { insert after … begin … end; }` over --mcp failed: `ped_update_document … undefined is not an object (evaluating 'u.$Type')`, with or without a note; a plain one-activity insert reproduced it. With that set removed, the insert landed but ped_check_errors reported `No action defined` on the new activity, and an inserted IF/ELSE came back wired to the wrong objects (the activity before it led into the else-branch log).
cause: flowPatchOps sent the whole insert as one update and addressed the elements it added in that same update by index: /flows/N/line/<end>ControlVector, /objectCollection/objects/N/action, …/relativeMiddlePoint, /flows/N/isErrorHandler. PED resolves a path against the document as it was before the update, so none of those reach the new element. A set below a new flow's line dereferences a line that is not there yet and fails the whole update. Any other set is accepted and lost, and so is the same property put in the constructor value (an ActionActivity's constructor takes only x/y/caption). Separately, several index-less appends to one array in one update are stored in reverse, and $id(/…/N) resolves against that final order, so with more than one new object every flow reference pointed at the wrong one.
insight: Two direct ped_update_document probes settle what an update can address, and they are cheaper than any reading of the code. First, add an element and set one of its properties in the same update, then read it back. Second, send the same set in a separate update. The difference is the whole bug. The separate-update set always landed: control vectors, action and isErrorHandler alike. So the fix is two updates. The first is all or nothing: the new elements, wired with $id(), and the stored elements moved to make room. The second fills in the new elements. A failed second update leaves an incomplete insert in Studio Pro, the same contract as CreateMicroflow's create-then-set. That is the price of 11.15, and the error says so. For ordering, give every add the array's stored length as its index; PED keeps adds at one shared index in listed order (its documented rule for inserting several elements at a position). The 1534 finding's 'an AnnotationFlow added before a SequenceFlow is stored after it' was this reversal, not something about annotation flows. A one-activity insert hides both bugs, because it adds one object and one flow, so verify with an insert of several elements (an IF/ELSE) and compare every flow's ends, sides and vectors against the same script run locally.
